title: Wastewater NPDES permit conditions practice questions
description: Free NPDES permit conditions practice questions on 40 CFR 122.2 and 122.41. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: How does 122.2 say an average weekly discharge limitation is calculated?

options.A: The highest single daily discharge measured during the week
options.B: The sum of all daily discharges measured during a calendar week divided by the number of daily discharges measured during that week
options.C: The sum of daily discharges over any 7 consecutive days divided by 7, whether or not each day was sampled
options.D: The total of all daily discharges measured during the week

questions.explanation: It is "the highest allowable average of "daily discharges" over a calendar week, calculated as the sum of all "daily discharges" measured during a calendar week divided by the number of "daily discharges" measured during that week."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What does 122.2 define a maximum daily discharge limitation to be?

options.A: The highest allowable average of daily discharges over a calendar month
options.B: The highest instantaneous reading allowed in any hour
options.C: The total discharge allowed over a calendar week
options.D: The highest allowable daily discharge

questions.explanation: "Maximum daily discharge limitation means the highest allowable "daily discharge.""

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: How does 122.2 define an indirect discharger?

options.A: A nondomestic discharger introducing pollutants to a publicly owned treatment works
options.B: Any discharger whose pipe is owned by a municipality
options.C: A POTW that discharges through a combined sewer system
options.D: A facility whose discharge reaches surface water only through ground water

questions.explanation: "Indirect discharger means a nondomestic discharger introducing "pollutants" to a "publicly owned treatment works."" The definition of discharge of a pollutant "does not include an addition of pollutants by any "indirect discharger.""

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Definitions: facilities, sludge and program terms
questions.question: Which of these does the 122.2 definition of sewage sludge list as included in sewage sludge?

options.A: Ash generated during the incineration of sewage sludge
options.B: Grit removed at the headworks
options.C: Scum, septage and portable toilet pumpings
options.D: Screenings removed from the influent

questions.explanation: Sewage sludge "includes, but is not limited to, solids removed during primary, secondary, or advanced waste water treatment, scum, septage, portable toilet pumpings"; it "does not include grit or screenings, or ash generated during the incineration of sewage sludge."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Definitions: facilities, sludge and program terms
questions.question: Under 122.2, who does "Director" normally mean when there is an approved State program?

options.A: The State Director
options.B: The EPA Administrator in every case
options.C: The superintendent of the POTW
options.D: The Regional Administrator in every case

questions.explanation: "When there is an approved State program, "Director" normally means the State Director." The definition adds that "in some circumstances, however, EPA retains the authority to take certain actions even when there is an approved State program."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Definitions: facilities, sludge and program terms
questions.question: Under 122.2, which of these is part of a "treatment works treating domestic sewage," regardless of ownership?

options.A: A septic tank serving a single home
options.B: A process wastewater sewer inside a factory
options.C: Land dedicated for the disposal of sewage sludge
options.D: A storm water outfall from a parking lot

questions.explanation: The term covers "a POTW or any other sewage sludge or waste water treatment devices or systems, regardless of ownership (including federal facilities), used in the storage, treatment, recycling, and reclamation of municipal or domestic sewage, including land dedicated for the disposal of sewage sludge." It "does not include septic tanks or similar devices."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.2, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Duty to comply and general conditions
questions.question: Under 122.41(a)(1), when must a permittee comply with section 307(a) toxic pollutant effluent standards and section 405(d) sewage sludge standards?

options.A: Only after the permit has been modified to include them
options.B: Within the time provided in the regulations that establish them, even if the permit has not yet been modified to incorporate the requirement
options.C: At the next permit renewal
options.D: Within 14 days after the Director sends written notice

questions.explanation: The permittee must comply "within the time provided in the regulations that establish these standards or prohibitions or standards for sewage sludge use or disposal, even if the permit has not yet been modified to incorporate the requirement."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Duty to comply and general conditions
questions.question: A permittee argues in an enforcement action that it would have had to halt or reduce the permitted activity to stay in compliance. What does 122.41(c) say about that argument?

options.A: It is an affirmative defense if supported by operating logs
options.B: It is a defense only for POTWs
options.C: It is a defense if the Director was told within 24 hours
options.D: It shall not be a defense

questions.explanation: "It shall not be a defense for a permittee in an enforcement action that it would have been necessary to halt or reduce the permitted activity in order to maintain compliance with the conditions of this permit."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Duty to comply and general conditions
questions.question: Under 122.41(e), when does the proper operation and maintenance condition require a permittee to operate back-up or auxiliary facilities it has installed?

options.A: At all times, as long as the permit is in effect
options.B: During every wet weather event
options.C: Whenever the Director inspects the facility
options.D: Only when the operation is necessary to achieve compliance with the conditions of the permit

questions.explanation: "This provision requires the operation of back-up or auxiliary facilities or similar systems which are installed by a permittee only when the operation is necessary to achieve compliance with the conditions of the permit."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Instead of the general 3-year retention period, which category of records does 122.41(j)(2) single out for retention of at least five years (or longer as required by 40 CFR part 503)?

options.A: Records of monitoring information required by the permit related to the permittee's sewage sludge use and disposal activities
options.B: Original strip chart recordings for continuous monitoring instrumentation
options.C: Calibration and maintenance records
options.D: Records of data used to complete the permit application

questions.explanation: Records "related to the permittee's sewage sludge use and disposal activities" are kept "for a period of at least five years (or longer as required by 40 CFR part 503)"; the other monitoring records, including calibration and maintenance records and strip charts, are kept "for a period of at least 3 years".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which item does 122.41(j)(3) list as part of the records of monitoring information?

options.A: The air temperature at the time of sampling
options.B: The cost of each analysis
options.C: The individual(s) who performed the analyses
options.D: The certification grade of the person who took the sample

questions.explanation: Records of monitoring information must include, among other items, "The individual(s) who performed the analyses" and "The analytical techniques or methods used".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 122.41(i), what must the Director or an authorized representative present before entering and inspecting the permittee's premises?

options.A: At least 48 hours of advance written notice
options.B: Credentials and other documents as may be required by law
options.C: Written consent from the facility's operator in charge
options.D: A copy of the facility's most recent DMR

questions.explanation: The permittee must allow the Director or an authorized representative, "upon presentation of credentials and other documents as may be required by law," to enter, have access to and copy records, inspect, and sample or monitor.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 122.41(l)(6)(i), the report on noncompliance which may endanger health or the environment shall contain several items. Which of these is one of them?

options.A: Steps taken or planned to reduce, eliminate, and prevent reoccurrence of the noncompliance
options.B: The name and certification number of the operator on duty
options.C: A cost estimate for the repairs
options.D: Copies of laboratory bench sheets for the previous 30 days

questions.explanation: "The report shall contain a description of the noncompliance and its cause; the period of noncompliance, including exact dates and times)," the anticipated time it is expected to continue if not corrected, "and steps taken or planned to reduce, eliminate, and prevent reoccurrence of the noncompliance."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For reports under 122.41(l)(6)(ii), what may the Director waive on a case-by-case basis, and on what condition?

options.A: The oral report, if the written report is received within 5 days
options.B: The written report, if the oral report has been received within 24 hours
options.C: Both reports, if the noncompliance lasted less than one day
options.D: The monthly DMR for that period, if the oral report was made

questions.explanation: "The Director may waive the written report on a case-by-case basis for reports under paragraph (l)(6)(ii) of this section if the oral report has been received within 24 hours."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What deadline does 122.41(l)(5) set for reports of compliance or noncompliance with interim and final requirements in a permit's compliance schedule?

options.A: Orally within 24 hours of each schedule date
options.B: Within 5 days of each schedule date
options.C: With the next annual permit renewal application
options.D: No later than 14 days following each schedule date

questions.explanation: Such reports "shall be submitted no later than 14 days following each schedule date."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these does the definition of severe property damage in 122.41(m)(1)(ii) expressly exclude?

options.A: Damage to the treatment facilities which causes them to become inoperable
options.B: Substantial and permanent loss of natural resources which can reasonably be expected to occur in the absence of a bypass
options.C: Economic loss caused by delays in production
options.D: Substantial physical damage to property

questions.explanation: "Severe property damage means substantial physical damage to property, damage to the treatment facilities which causes them to become inoperable, or substantial and permanent loss of natural resources which can reasonably be expected to occur in the absence of a bypass. Severe property damage does not mean economic loss caused by delays in production."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: One condition for a bypass to escape the prohibition in 122.41(m)(4)(i) is that there were no feasible alternatives. When does that rule say this condition is not satisfied?

options.A: When the bypass lasted longer than 24 hours
options.B: When the permittee gave notice less than ten days ahead
options.C: When adequate back-up equipment should have been installed in the exercise of reasonable engineering judgment to prevent a bypass during normal equipment downtime or preventive maintenance
options.D: When the bypass was caused by wet weather

questions.explanation: "This condition is not satisfied if adequate back-up equipment should have been installed in the exercise of reasonable engineering judgment to prevent a bypass which occurred during normal periods of equipment downtime or preventive maintenance".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 122.41(n)(2), an upset is an affirmative defense to an action for noncompliance with which kind of limitations?

options.A: Technology based permit effluent limitations
options.B: Water quality-based effluent limitations
options.C: Monitoring and reporting conditions of the permit
options.D: Standards for sewage sludge use or disposal

questions.explanation: "An upset constitutes an affirmative defense to an action brought for noncompliance with such technology based permit effluent limitations if the requirements of paragraph (n)(3) of this section are met."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A permittee wants to establish the affirmative defense of upset. Under 122.41(n)(3), which of these must it demonstrate through properly signed, contemporaneous operating logs, or other relevant evidence?

options.A: That the upset lasted less than 24 hours
options.B: That no Industrial User discharged to the facility during the upset
options.C: That the facility had no other upset during the permit term
options.D: That the permitted facility was at the time being properly operated

questions.explanation: The permittee "shall demonstrate, through properly signed, contemporaneous operating logs, or other relevant evidence that", among other things, "The permitted facility was at the time being properly operated". It must also show that "An upset occurred and that the permittee can identify the cause(s) of the upset", that it gave the 24-hour notice, and that it complied with any required remedial measures.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 122.41, Conditions applicable to all permits (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 122.41(n)(4), who has the burden of proof in an enforcement proceeding where an upset is claimed?

options.A: The Director bringing the action
options.B: The permittee seeking to establish the occurrence of an upset
options.C: The EPA Administrator
options.D: Whoever filed the original complaint

questions.explanation: "In any enforcement proceeding the permittee seeking to establish the occurrence of an upset has the burden of proof."
